boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces documented for studying, collaboration, student activities, arts, and cultural programming.

cards.title: Stony Brook Union
cards.subtitle: Central campus • open study and service spaces
cards.notes: Use the main lobby’s powered seating for a study break, then check the building directory for student-facing offices and campus resources.
cards.short_summary: A renovated central hub with lobby study seating and student services.
cards.evidence_claim: The Union has three levels of student-centric spaces, and its main lobby supports studying and collaborative learning with comfortable seating and powered stations.
cards.source_title: Union Building Highlights | Campus Life Centers
cards.access_notes: Campus building; consult Campus Life Centers for current building access and room availability.

cards.title: Club Hub
cards.subtitle: Stony Brook Union • student lounge
cards.notes: Stop in for the lounge’s games or crafting area, and use it as a meeting point before a registered club program or campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A Union gathering space with games, crafting space, seating, and club storage.
cards.evidence_claim: Club Hub is a 6,500-square-foot gathering space with video games, billiards, air hockey, crafting space, seating, and club storage.
cards.source_title: Union Building Highlights | Campus Life Centers
cards.access_notes: Located within the Stony Brook Union; observe posted lounge and event rules.

cards.title: Student Activities Center (SAC)
cards.subtitle: Academic Mall • gathering and event building
cards.notes: Meet classmates in the main lobby or look for a scheduled lecture, movie, concert, or student-organization activity in the building.
cards.short_summary: A central Academic Mall building built around student gathering, events, and amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The SAC is a focal point and gathering place with four levels of student-centric spaces; its events include lectures, movies, concerts, and recognition ceremonies.
cards.source_title: Student Activities Center Building Highlights | Campus Life Centers
cards.access_notes: Campus building; events and room use vary by schedule.

cards.title: Charles B. Wang Center
cards.subtitle: Campus cultural center • gardens, programs, and exhibitions
cards.notes: Walk through the building’s gardens and galleries, then check the Wang Center calendar for a public cultural program, film, lecture, or exhibition.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive campus cultural center designed for exhibitions, performances, films, lectures, and celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wang Center contains gardens and spaces for conferences, performances, films, lectures, exhibitions, and cultural celebrations.
cards.source_title: About the Charles B. Wang Center
cards.access_notes: Public programming and gallery access vary by event and building schedule.

cards.title: East Hall’s Bamboo Garden
cards.subtitle: Charles B. Wang Center • indoor garden hall
cards.notes: Pause in the skylit hall to take in the bamboo garden, then pair the visit with a Wang Center exhibition, lecture, or cultural event.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled Wang Center hall with an indoor bamboo garden.
cards.evidence_claim: East Hall at the Wang Center has a bamboo garden with a skylight and accommodates lectures and performances.
cards.source_title: Wang Conference Center | Conference Event Services
cards.access_notes: Part of the Wang Center; respect any event setup or access controls.

cards.title: Staller Center for the Arts
cards.subtitle: Arts campus • performances, films, and gallery
cards.notes: Check the calendar before heading over for a performance or film, and leave time to look through the University Art Gallery when it is open.
cards.short_summary: An arts venue with theaters, films, departmental events, and a University Art Gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: Staller Center presents professional performances and hundreds of Art, Theater Arts, and Music events, and includes five theaters and a 5,000-square-foot University Art Gallery.
cards.access_notes: Performance, film, and gallery availability depend on the current schedule; some programs may require tickets.

cards.title: North Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Frank Melville, Jr. Memorial Library • quiet and collaborative seating
cards.notes: Choose individual, pair, or group seating for coursework, and reserve a collaboration room in advance when your group needs a dedicated workspace.
cards.short_summary: A large library reading room with technology, varied seating, and reservable group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The North Reading Room offers individual, pair, and group seating, 12 group study rooms, workstations, printing, scanning, and screen sharing.
cards.source_title: Places to study | Stony Brook University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Study rooms require online booking and are available to current students; check library hours before visiting.

cards.title: Central Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Frank Melville, Jr. Memorial Library • study and current periodicals
cards.notes: Settle into individual or group seating, browse current newspapers in the reading nook, or reserve a collaborative room for project work.
cards.short_summary: A library community space with study seating, periodicals, event space, and collaborative rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Central Reading Room has individual, pair, and group seating, a reading nook with current newspapers and magazines, and collaborative group study rooms.
cards.source_title: Places to study | Stony Brook University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Collaborative rooms are bookable by current students; confirm library hours and reservation requirements.

cards.title: Melville Library Galleria
cards.subtitle: Frank Melville, Jr. Memorial Library • first-floor collaborative corridor
cards.notes: Use the first-floor seating for a short collaborative session between classes, keeping the space clear for the library’s peak-traffic flow.
cards.short_summary: A skylit first-floor library corridor set up as a collaborative area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Galleria is a light-filled first-floor corridor with four-story ceilings and skylights, described by the Libraries as a bustling collaborative area.
cards.source_title: Places to study | Stony Brook University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open during applicable library building hours; it is a shared circulation area.

cards.title: Melville Library Second Floor Core
cards.subtitle: Frank Melville, Jr. Memorial Library • silent study area
cards.notes: Enter through the North Reading Room when you need a quiet solo session, and keep conversations and group work for the library’s collaborative zones.
cards.short_summary: A quiet library core near science, engineering, maps, and government-information collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Second Floor Core is accessed through the North Reading Room and is a quiet study area housing science and engineering materials, maps, and government information.
cards.source_title: Places to study | Stony Brook University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located inside Melville Library; confirm library hours before visiting.
